## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `event-quantile-recency`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-14T05:25:41.723Z.

Signal candidate (44) — event-quantile recency: express how recent an item is as its position in the workspace's own recorded event stream, not as elapsed wall-clock time. Measured 2026-08-14.

Candidates (39) through (43) all take the candidate set as given and ask how to score or how to cut it. This candidate changes the unit one of the oldest signals is denominated in, and it is proposed because the roadmap declares a target range no fitted constant can cover.

## The problem the current unit has

Recency today is elapsed time against a half-life. A half-life is a constant, and pm-sxyj1v already owns the finding that every behavioural constant in this product was fitted to this one corpus and declares nothing about the population it was fitted on. For recency the consequence is sharper than for the others, because the declared target range spans two extremes that no single constant serves.

pm-z436 describes a workspace minutes old holding three items. pm-e5yupa describes a workspace whose oldest format version must still be readable after decades. pm-g2zz describes a million items. A half-life tuned so that yesterday outranks last week is, on the three-item scratch project, a constant that ranks every item identically because they were all created inside one minute; and on the thirty-year corpus it is a constant under which everything before last quarter is indistinguishable from the origin.

The signal is not wrong in either case. It is uninformative in both, and it is uninformative for the same reason: the unit is external to the workspace being ranked.

## The proposal

Rank recency by the number of recorded events between an item's last relevant event and the head of the workspace's event stream, then normalize by the total event count. An item touched at event 9,900 of 10,000 has recency 0.99. An item touched at event 100 has recency 0.01. Elapsed time never enters.

Three properties follow without tuning.

It is scale-invariant. The same expression serves three items spanning ninety seconds and a million items spanning thirty years, because both are measured against their own stream length. There is no constant to fit and therefore no corpus to fit it on.

It tracks activity rather than the calendar. A project dormant for a year and then worked on for a week has a recency ordering that reflects the week, which is what a returning agent needs, and which a wall-clock half-life reports as one year of uniform staleness. This is the property pm-bwyw asks for directly.

It is robust to the defect pm-07pt16 owns. That item found that recency computed from updated_at is erased by the governance writes this project mandates, because a metadata backfill bumps the timestamp of work nobody touched. Under event quantiles the same backfill still moves the item, so this candidate does not fix pm-07pt16 and must not be described as fixing it. What it does is make the damage bounded and countable: a bulk pass of N writes displaces every untouched item by exactly N stream positions, which is a quantity the record can report and a filter can discount, whereas a timestamp overwrite destroys the prior value.

## Degeneracy clauses, which are mandatory for entry in this catalog

On a workspace with one recorded event every item has quantile 1.0, the signal is uniform, and the ranking degenerates to whatever the other signals say. It never refuses and never errors.

On a workspace where every item was touched exactly once and never again, the quantile ordering is the creation ordering, which is the correct answer and not a degeneracy.

It is a reordering signal only. It has no capacity to admit an item the candidate generator did not produce, and it cannot raise any declared ceiling.

## What must be measured before this is promoted

Whether the event stream is dense enough to discriminate. On this corpus the history holds tens of thousands of entries across 2,484 items, so quantiles are fine-grained. On a workspace with three items and nine events the quantile takes nine distinct values, which is adequate. The failure mode to look for is the opposite one: a workspace where a single automated writer produces most events, in which case quantiles measure the writer's cadence rather than the project's. That is a real risk here specifically, because this project's own automation is a heavy writer, and it is the reason this is a candidate and not a decision.

Routed through pm-g8t7b9 like every other entry in this catalog. Do not weight it on the strength of this note.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
